## Trial `boot-kernel-parameter-rhel7__b3fiM96`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor directly demonstrated the full required transition: a healthy pre-change baseline without audit=1, application of the parameter via grubby to all boot entries plus /etc/default/grub for future regenerations, a safe/acknowledged reboot, a genuinely changed boot_id proving an actual restart, and a post-reboot cmdline/dmesg confirmation that audit=1 was active on the newly booted kernel. Both material outcomes (boot-time setting and persistence across reboot) are satisfied with direct, coherent evidence.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.930 | 9/2 (+1 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Kernel boots with audit=1 on node1
  - **Why:** Baseline /proc/cmdline lacked audit=1 (cmd-609cecf5e86a4942). grubby --update-kernel=ALL --args=audit=1 applied audit=1 to both the main and rescue kernel entries, confirmed via grubby --info=ALL (cmd-01516c1e9bd14cdc). After an actual reboot (boot_id changed from 2fc81aed... to 6967ac42..., confirmed across cmd-3202f4b192c0404d/cmd-995dfe09d1c84666/cmd-d183666f9e0a4610), the post-reboot /proc/cmdline shows audit=1 and dmesg logs 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' (cmd-a16108b376ad40b9), directly demonstrating the setting took effect on a genuinely restarted kernel.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-609cecf5e86a4942`, `cmd-01516c1e9bd14cdc`, `cmd-341ca93976e346a6`, `cmd-3202f4b192c0404d`, `cmd-995dfe09d1c84666`, `cmd-d183666f9e0a4610`, `cmd-a16108b376ad40b9`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** Setting persists across reboots (not just the running kernel)
  - **Why:** grubby updated all boot entries (main+rescue) rather than just the current session, and /etc/default/grub GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX was also updated with audit=1 so future grub2-mkconfig regenerations preserve it; /boot/grub2/grub.cfg was confirmed to already contain audit=1 on both linux16 lines (cmd-33b4c69d9148461e). A real reboot then showed the same parameter present in the post-reboot cmdline and dmesg, directly confirming persistence across the boot rather than relying on configuration alone.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-33b4c69d9148461e`, `cmd-a16108b376ad40b9`, `cmd-d183666f9e0a4610`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. All state-changing commands map cleanly to the task: grubby update (cmd-01516c1e9bd14cdc), /etc/default/grub sed edit (cmd-33b4c69d9148461e), and the reboot itself (cmd-341ca93976e346a6) were all necessary to implement and verify the persistent kernel parameter. Discovery commands (cmd-cef882a6d8ea4b04, cmd-e81ede3c6af24d44, cmd-f0351817bf70443e) were read-only. One minor residue: the backgrounded reboot mechanism left /tmp/reboot.log on node1 (visible in after_executor temporary-files snapshot) which was never cleaned up; this is bounded, low-risk, and a normal byproduct of a controlled reboot, but it is unremoved residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-341ca93976e346a6`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`
